Commentary.Commentary: ... RUN CHASE ...

South Africa were decent too on this batting track. They knew it wasn't going to be easy on this wicket but their bowlers stuck to the plans and chipped in with wickets at regular intervals. Ottneil Baartman and Andile Phehlukwayo took two wickets each but the pick of the bowers was Lizaad Williams who scalped 4 wickets. South Africa have batted well this series but haven't chased a score yet. This would be a different test for their batters but they are in good form so expect them to take the game all the way. Stay tuned for the chase.

For the first time Ireland have batted their full quota in this series and they have done reasonably well too. The top four made a massive contributions. Starting with the openers who struggled previously but today they added 100 runs on top. Andy Balbirnie looked rusty for his 45 while Paul Stirling was at his best as he fell just short of 12 for his ton. Curtis Campher thrn played a handy innings however, it was Tector's valuable innings that helped Ireland get past 280.
A single to end then! Fuller and outside off. This is lofte down to long off for one. End of a really good last over.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set. The players are out in the middle. Paul Stirling and Andy Balbirnie to open for Ireland. Lungi Ngidi to bowl first.
Rassie van der Dussen says it is a different challenge, bowling first and hopes to do well with the new ball. Tells Babuma has Test cricket coming up so nothing really big. Informs the team changes.

Paul Stirling says they will bat first and put some runs on the board. Tells toss is always 50-50. Shares they have not shown improvement in both games and want to do well in this game. South Africa (Playing XI) - Ryan Rickelton (WK), Reeza Hendricks (In for Temba Bavuma), Rassie van der Dussen (C), Kyle Verreynne, Tristan Stubbs, Jason Smith (In for Wiaan Mulder), Andile Phehlukwayo, Bjorn Fortuin, Lizaad Williams, Lungi Ngidi, Ottneil Baartman.
Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling (C), Andy Balbirnie, Curtis Campher, Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker (WK), George Dockrell, Mark Adair, Matthew Humphreys, Craig Young, Graham Hume, Fionn Hand.
TOSS - Ireland have won the toss and will BAT first!

Ireland have been beaten in both the games but the way they lost is a big concern for them. They lost both the games by more than 100 runs and their batting stumbled as both times they failed to bat the 50-over quota. Although in both matches there was pressure of chasing down a huge total. Ireland will hope they can showcase a better quality with the bat. South Africa on the other hand have ticked all the boxes. Everyone have performed well and will hope they end the series in a similar fashion. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

Hello and welcome to the third and final ODI between South Africa and Ireland. The Proteas have taken an unassailable lead of 2-0 in the series and will look to end it with a clean sweep whereas Ireland will hope they can take something away from this series and avoid whitewash. With the series already sealed, expect a couple of alterations from either side as both will try and test their bench strength in this game. Stay tuned.
...MATCH DAY...

After two dominant performances, South Africa are set to face Ireland once again in the third and final ODI of this 3-match series, with the Proteas eyeing a clean sweep to secure a 3-0 result. The action will unfold at the Sheikh Zayed Stadium in Abu Dhabi, where Ireland will be eager to put up a stronger fight and salvage some pride to end the series. In both previous games, Ireland faltered with the bat while chasing, losing by significant margins. Despite promising starts, their batters failed to capitalize and build meaningful partnerships, which will be crucial as they head into this final match. The top four batters, in particular, must take on the bulk of the responsibility, leveraging their experience to give the team the much-needed momentum. The bowling unit, led by Mark Adair, Craig Young and Andy McBrine has performed well, but they’ll need stronger support from the rest of the attack to contain South Africa’s potent batting lineup. On the other hand, South Africa may have a couple of injury concerns that could alter their team combination, but with the series already sealed, a few changes are likely as they aim to give players valuable game time. Ryan Rickelton and Tristan Stubbs have been in excellent form and will look to carry their momentum into this final match. The bowlers have also played a key role, with Lizaad Williams leading the attack and receiving strong support from Lungi Ngidi and Bjorn Fortuin. With momentum on their side, South Africa are clear favourites to win the final game. However, Ireland still possess the ability to pull off an upset and prove their mettle. It will be a tough challenge, but if they can put together a collective team effort, an upset isn't beyond their reach.
